I farm only 6 mu, so I will keep the whole field in the wheat-maize rotation and not split it. I have done this for 15 years, I have well irrigation, and with a seven-person household I need steady grain output more than experimentation. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough fertilizer on to secure tillering and grain filling, irrigate a few key times, and manage weeds and disease with limited but timely sprays. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same 6 mu, using hybrid seed because I value stronger yield and stability in the summer season. I will keep fertilizer moderate but sufficient, irrigate when the crop is most sensitive, and do a small number of pesticide sprays to control the main seasonal risks. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it fits my scale, my equipment conditions, and the wheat-maize system, and it lets me turn the land around quickly between crops.
